findings.description: Reviewed_ids cannot express which profile was reviewed, and in this corpus that is a live ambiguity rather than a theoretical one. review.schema.json allows exactly artifact_id, revision and digest in each reviewed_ids item, with additionalProperties false, so there is no profile field. Every artifact FB2-REV-000001 claims to have reviewed exists in BOTH the as_is and the synthetic_reference profile with different content. Only the digest disambiguates them, and only because the digest is a real content hash. Of the 16 recorded digests that could be re-checked against current content, all 16 match the as_is file byte for byte and none matches the corresponding synthetic_reference file, so the prior record is correct on those. It is structurally fragile: a reader applying an artifact_id to the wrong profile would review different content while believing they had reviewed the reviewed one. The review records authored by this pass state the profile span explicitly in their scope field to compensate; the prior record does not.
findings.evidence: review.schema.json reviewed_ids.items properties are artifact_id, revision, digest with additionalProperties false. 16 of the prior record's 17 digests equal the sha256 of the as_is file and differ from the synthetic_reference file. The 17th, for FB2-VER-EXE-000001, is now stale - see FB2-REV-FND-000174.

findings.description: The prior review's dispositions use resolved_artifact_id to point at the artifact each finding is raised against rather than at an artifact created to resolve it. The schema documents the field as 'Optional ID of artifact created to resolve this finding'. Example: finding FB2-FND-000001 is raised against FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 and dispositioned 'accepted' with resolved_artifact_id 'FB2-SAF-FSR-000001'. The same self-referential pattern appears in all five dispositions. No artifact was created to resolve any of the five findings, so a reader could conclude that resolving artifacts exist when none do. Recorded, not corrected: FB2-REV-000001 was not modified.

findings.description: Structural gap in the review framework, discovered while attempting this very meta review: review.schema.json constrains reviewed_ids[].artifact_id and findings[].artifact_id to a three-segment pattern, but review artifact ids have only two segments. The consequence is that no review record can legally list another review record as a reviewed artifact or as the subject of a finding, so review-record quality is structurally outside the review framework meant to cover it. A reader relying on automated_review_coverage would see every review record counted and every review record uncheckable. The workaround used here is to audit the prior review through the artifacts it covered, which is weaker: it cannot bind a finding to the review record itself. No schema was edited and no check was weakened.
findings.evidence: Observed directly: writing a review record with 'FB2-REV-000001' in reviewed_ids produced 7 high-severity schema findings from corpus.py ('schema violation at reviewed_ids/0/artifact_id'). The artifact base schema permits one to three segments via '^FB2(-[A-Z]{2,4}){1,3}-[0-9]{6}$', so review ids are legal as ids but cannot be referenced by review records.

findings.description: The corpus's automated_review_coverage dimension cannot observe review records other than one. corpus.py computes the numerator by loading a single hardcoded file, docs/artifacts/reviews/records/review-vertical-slice.json, and reading only its reviewed_ids. Every other review record in docs/artifacts/reviews/records/ is indexed as an artifact, so it enlarges the DENOMINATOR while contributing nothing to the numerator. This pass demonstrates the effect: adding eleven review records moved the dimension from 17/87 to 17/101 while the numerator stayed at 17. The metric therefore reports review coverage getting worse as review coverage improves, which is the opposite of its intent. The reviewed_by trace links added by this pass carry the information the dimension was meant to express, but the dimension does not read them. No tool change was made: corpus.py is outside this review's write scope and editing a metric to look better would be metric gaming.
findings.evidence: corpus.py line 903: rp = self.artifacts_dir / 'reviews' / 'records' / 'review-vertical-slice.json'; line 905-906: reviewed_ids populated only from that file's reviewed_ids; line 908-909: numerator = len(reviewed_ids & index_ids), denominator = len(index_ids). No other code path aggregates reviewed_ids for this dimension.

revision_history.description: Provenance repair by a separate session (opencode-2026-10-01-provenance-repair), not a re-review. All 14 reviewed_ids digests in this record were re-derived from the artefact files as they stand on disk in the correct profile (as_is).  14 of 14 named artefacts have been revised or had their bytes replaced since this review was issued, so this record is re-issued at revision 2 and its digest for those artefacts now names the current revision; per-artefact detail, including the superseded digest and the basis for each classification, is in digest_corrections.  The findings, dispositions, scope, checklist and reviewer_identity of the original pass are untouched by this repair. The digest refresh does not carry the weight of a re-review: the original reviewer session did not examine the current revision of the revised artefacts, and no substantive re-examination was performed here.

record_verbatim.scope: SCOPE IS PARTIAL AND DELIBERATELY SO. This record audits the prior review FB2-REV-000001. The review schema does not permit FB2-REV-000001 itself to appear in reviewed_ids or in a findings[].artifact_id: review.schema.json constrains both to '^FB2-[A-Z]{2,3}-[A-Z]{2,3}-[0-9]{6}$', which requires three dash-separated segments, while a review artifact id has only two. A review of a review record is structurally unrepresentable and is recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000184 rather than worked around. To audit a review record at all, this meta review necessarily re-covers the artifacts that review declared; that re-coverage is enumerated below and is a schema limitation, not additional coverage. FB2-VER-EXE-000001 is excluded because it was revised to revision 2 by a concurrent session during this pass and its content has moved; it is the subject of FB2-REV-FND-000174 in FB2-REV-000010. This record does not review itself.
record_verbatim.title: Meta review: audit of the prior review FB2-REV-000001's claims against the artifacts it covered

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-REV-000011` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. NEVER record the approval in revision_history - doing so stales every link pinning this revision and invalidates every stored review digest. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.

target.primary_key_rule: ID-RULE-004-A1: an artefact identifier is unique within its profile; two records of different profiles may carry the same identifier string.
